title: I built a Cultivation World Simulator where every NPC is an LLM Agent. (Open source and free)
author: Sudden_Ad_1888
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I'm working on Cultivation World Simulator, an open-source project that combines LLMs with the Xianxia/Cultivation genre.

Unlike traditional RPGs where you play as a single character, here you play as the "Heavenly Dao" (God/The Will of the World). You don't just grind levels; you observe and intervene in the lives of AI cultivators, witness the rise and fall of sects, and shape the history of the world.

Key Features:

LLM-Driven NPCs: Every cultivator is an autonomous AI agent. They have their own personalities, retain memories of interactions, and make decisions based on their own logic.

God-Tier Gameplay: As the Heavenly Dao, you can drop artifacts, trigger tribulations, or secretly guide a chosen one to see how they react.

Emergent Storytelling: Sect wars, betrayals, and alliances happen dynamically based on AI interactions.

🛠️ Technical Requirements (Important):

Because the game logic is driven by AI, please be aware of the following:

Bring Your Own Key: You will need to provide your own LLM API Key (e.g., OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, etc.) to run the game.

Token Usage: Be aware that token usage can be high. The game continuously simulates NPC thoughts, dialogues, and world events, which adds up.

Local LLM Support: You CAN run this locally (via Ollama, etc.) to save money. However, the model needs to be smart enough.

Recommendation: Do not use tiny models. Dumber models will likely break the game loop or hallucinate nonsensically.

Status:

✅ Free & Open Source: The game client itself is free. Code is on GitHub.

✅ Playable Demo: Available now.

✅ English Support: English version is live!

⚠️ Disclaimer:

The project is in active development, so bugs are expected. Also, the English localization is currently AI-translated, so some cultivation terms might feel a bit "raw." (Since I am not a native English speaker)

Feedback is welcome!

**Github Links:** [Cultivation World Simulator](https://github.com/AI-Cultivation/cultivation-world-simulator/blob/main/EN_README.md)

comments.author: 0bscuris
comments.body:
Fascinating. 

When messing around with the idea of llms as npc’s, i just had the llm run the dialogue but found that it was way too hard to keep coherently in the intended design. They would spiral out really easy, get off topic. 

Breaking it up into thoughts first, then dialogue derived from those thoughts is a nice break point to check to make sure their thoughts make sense in the greater story, before they speak to the player.

replies.author: Sudden_Ad_1888
replies.body: that's exactly what i thought and felt when i was playing games like ai dungeon etc.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body:
In thinking down this path you’ve introduced to me. 

Maybe the middle ground here between current static dialogue trees and llm wildness is, the player gets the freedom to say what they want, the llm generates the npc’s “thought” based on the players input, that thought is checked for appropriateness in someway, maybe a “rules agent.” 

then using that thought the llm picks the dialogue closest to that thought from 10?ish, predetermined responses that are hardcoded in so a human has looked at them and they make sense. 

Including a response like, “r u insane?” If the player tries to trick the llm into leaving the story. 

It would feel more free than picking option dialogue option a, b, c then npc responding d but not quite the open ended insanity of a llm.

replies.author: Xthebuilder
replies.body: Have you thought about using LLM as judge ? It could help you set a standard for what type of responses are similar , you could use an embedding model and have like a loose semantic match so the conversation is relevant but not so strict
